CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: intervertebral disc

2 of 2 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 0 fall below it; 0 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

  • glycosaminoglycan (GAG) - exchangeable -OH pool per disaccharide unit: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)
  • mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT) - exchangeable amide-proton-equivalent: ✓ detectable (both)

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] glycogen (glycoCEST): searched explicitly ('intervertebral disc glycoCEST glycogen concentration'); the disc is avascular and not a glycogen-storing tissue - no endogenous glycogen evidence found; ABSENT, not a CEST target here.; [model's own exclusion] glucose: disc is hypoxic/anaerobic but no source reported a tissue-internal glucose concentration >1 mM; glucose values are FE-model transport/uptake estimates (PMID 39366140) or ex vivo culture medium (e.g. 25 mM, PMID 41969531), not stored tissue-internal assays - fails the >1 mM tissue-internal bar.; [model's own exclusion] lactate: same as glucose - only appears in transport/FE models (max lactate at cartilage endplate, PMID 39366140), no direct tissue-internal >1 mM assay value found.; [model's own exclusion] creatine / taurine / glutathione: search returned no results for a stored tissue-internal >1 mM disc value.; [model's own exclusion] collagen I / collagen II (as standalone species): chemically defined but highly rigid; only a small mobile amide fraction is CEST-active and that is already folded into the APT protein pool; no separate direct mM amide number reported.; [model's own exclusion] proteoglycan/aggrecan (as whole molecule): the relevant CEST-active sub-pool is the GAG disaccharide (reported above); the aggrecan core-protein amide contribution is folded into the APT pool; reporting aggrecan as a single huge molecule's molarity would be the wrong number for CEST.; [model's own exclusion] inorganic phosphate / ATP / phosphocreatine: 31P MRS category labels and 31P-only resonances, off-target for 1H CEST; no >1 mM 1H-relevant quantified value found.; [model's own exclusion] water: the CEST acceptor pool, not an exchangeable-proton source target by the rules.

glycosaminoglycan (GAG) - exchangeable -OH pool per disaccharide unit — CEST: ✓ detectable (chemical exchange)

Concentration: 300.00 mM typical (~100-500 mM (estimated, -OH-equivalent per disaccharide unit))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: ESTIMATE, not a measured mM. GAG is the dominant dry component of nucleus pulposus ECM (cited PMIDs confirm GAG/proteoglycan as the major NP component and the gagCEST target). Assuming healthy NP ~89% water (PMID 39012562: 88.8% in porcine NP) and ~60% of the ~10% dry mass being GAG, with a GAG disaccharide-unit mass ~600 g/mol: per 100 mL tissue, dry ~10 g, GAG ~6 g -> ~10 mmol of disaccharide units -> ~100 mM unit-equivalent in wet tissue; at 85-90% water this is on the order of 100-500 mM. The gagCEST -OH pool = ~3-4 exchangeable hydroxyls per disaccharide unit. Central estimate ~300 mM of -OH-equivalent.

Recommended field strength(s): 0.5 T, 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (sugary / side-chain hydroxyl -OH (alcoholic, per disaccharide) [hydroxyl]: concentration 100-500 mM, kex fixed at 600 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown)) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 1.54-6.95%, 1.5 T: 3.15-13.35%, 3 T: 7.17-25.39%, 5 T: 12.77-38.44%, 7 T: 17.23-46.87%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis: The 0.825 ppm OH pool has no near-collision with the APT amide (3.5 ppm) at 3-7 T. The persistent overlap warning is only vs the semisolid MT pool (-2.4 ppm), expected for an ~1 ppm OH pool. At 0.5 T the GAG-amide and APT-amide (both 3.5 ppm) fully blur (0 Hz). The GAG amide and APT amide are therefore indistinguishable at all fields - a combined amide peak, not two.

Direct water saturation: Direct-sat bandwidths (10.6-42.6 Hz) are far below the OH offset in Hz at 3-7 T, so direct water saturation does not mask the OH pool. At 0.5 T the 0.825 ppm offset (~2.4 Hz) is comparable to the 10.6 Hz band, so low-field OH contrast is partially direct-saturation-contaminated.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: The OH kex=600 s−1 was borrowed from myo-inositol (PMID 20951217, human brain in vivo), not measured for GAG in disc. The shift is from a GAG phantom (PMID 30230599) and one cartilage study (PMID 21460030). A 600 s−1 OH rate is fast exchange; the real GAG OH in the dense, acidic disc (pH 5-7, macromolecular crowding) may differ substantially, so the 4-37% contrast is an upper-bound-ish estimate. Lower confidence.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 4.392% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 8.672% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=750 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — OH pool at kex~600 s−1 is fast exchange; low-moderate B1 (0.75 µT) minimizes direct water saturation spill while 750 ms reaches quasi-steady state. Matches PMID 27439061 optimum (0.8 µT, 1.0 s). High field separates OH from MT tail.
    recommended sequence: 17.940% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=750 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Higher B0 spreads the OH offset from the MT tail in Hz, so slightly higher B1 (1.0 µT) is tolerable without losing exchange contrast to direct saturation. 750 ms sustains quasi-steady state.
    recommended sequence: 29.156% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — At 7 T the OH offset in Hz is well clear of the MT tail, so 1.0 µT is safe and 1000 ms Tsat pushes the fast-exchange pool to full steady state for max contrast.
    recommended sequence: 36.995% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: Swept B1 (0.25-1.0 µT) and Tsat (500-1000 ms) sit in low-B1, intermediate-exchange regime. The OH pool is exchange-broadened and overlaps the MT tail, so MTRasym is inadequate; AREX (B1-normalized MTR) or Lorentzian-difference/multi-pool fitting is preferred to separate GAG OH from MT and APT. PMID 33475842 used exactly this multi-pool Z-fitting (GAG+APT+NOE+MT+direct) for lumbar discs. PMID 27439061 optimum (0.8 µT, 1.0 s) matches the sweep.

Potential clinical impact

No verified disease application of this pool's CEST/NOE signal was found. Searched gagCEST disc degeneration, cervical/lumbar disc, scoliosis, spondyloarthritis, leg length discrepancy, plus non-CEST GAG content in rabbit, dog, bovine and mouse IVDD. Sufficient CEST and metabolite-change evidence found for musculoskeletal disc disease.

Caveats / critique (6 points, 347 words) — Concentration of 300 mM per disaccharide is a rough proxy for NP GAG density, an effective equivalent not a molar count. Literature gagCEST targets the NP, the …
  • Concentration of 300 mM per disaccharide is a rough proxy for NP GAG density, an effective equivalent not a molar count. Literature gagCEST targets the NP, the GAG-rich compartment, so compartment choice is right. MTRasym in PMID 26583472 (2.92% Pfirrmann 1-2) is NOT clean GAG contrast - it is bulk Z-asymmetry dominated by MT/NOE. Do not transcribe as GAG contrast.
  • Hydroxyl class correct; -OH pool is the genuine gagCEST feature and the right CEST target. Amide class and 3.5 ppm estimate reasonable for the N-acetyl backbone. The glycoNOE rNOE group is correctly NOT simulated - 13 protons violates the per-repeating-unit rule, so no contrast is claimable for it. No amine/guanidinium group exists, so none neglected.
  • N-acetyl CH3 (~-1 ppm) overlaps glycoNOE and is non-exchangeable. gagCEST literature and PMID 30230599/21460030 place the GAG OH pool near 0.65-1.0 ppm in vivo, consistent with the 0.825 ppm shift. In-vivo shift may drift with low pH of degenerate discs (pH 5-7 in PMID 27670140), so 0.825 ppm is a healthy-disc value only.
  • N-acetyl CH3 (rNOE ~-1 ppm) and glycoNOE sugar-ring C-H are non-exchangeable and correctly excluded. Carboxylate/sulfate carry no proton. No exchangeable group missing. Groups not simulated: glycoNOE / aliphatic C-H (sugar ring C-H + N-acetyl CH3, per disaccharide) [rnoe] -- not simulated: glycosaminoglycan (GAG) - exchangeable -OH pool per disaccharide unit: n_exchangeable_protons=13 is not a per-molecule (or per-repeating-unit) proton count.
  • Use 1-12; for a polymer or macromolecular pool give the concentration PER repeating unit (e.g. glycogen ~250-300 mM glucosyl units x 3 hydroxyl protons; the mobile-protein amide pool ~200-300 mM x 1), not a whole-molecule count. no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor
  • Repeating unit: GAG disaccharide (chondroitin sulfate / keratan sulfate). n_exchangeable_protons = 3-4 hydroxyl per unit (gagCEST ~4.5 ppm) plus amide/N-acetyl. Concentration reported per disaccharide-unit (-OH-equivalent), NOT per aggrecan macro-molecule. Primary, well-established disc CEST target. mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT) - exchangeable amide-proton-equivalent — CEST: ✓ detectable (both)

Concentration: 250.00 mM typical (~200-300 mM (estimated, amide-proton-equivalent))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: ESTIMATE, not a measured mM. APT CEST is a real, quantifiable pH-sensitive contrast measured in the disc (PMIDs 33475842, 42286353 confirm a measurable APT signal). No source gives amide mM directly. The disc ECM is protein-rich (type II collagen in NP, type I in AF, PMID 22389123); the mobile (non-rigid) peptide/protein backbone contributes the APT pool. By analogy to the general APT literature, the mobile amide-proton-equivalent concentration in dense tissues is ~200-300 mM (1 exchangeable amide proton per equivalent unit). Rigid, cross-linked collagen contributes little. Central estimate ~250 mM of amide-proton-equivalent.

Recommended field strength(s): 0.5 T, 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (aliphatic C-H side-chain pool (mobile protein, per residue) [rnoe]: concentration 200-300 mM, kex fixed at 5 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown); backbone amide -NH- (mobile protein/peptide, per residue) [amide]: concentration 200-300 mM, kex 15-158 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 2.71-3.99%, 1.5 T: 4.47-6.56%, 3 T: 1.63-11.53%, 5 T: 1.93-13.36%, 7 T: 2.09-14.29%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • The 3.5 ppm amide fully collides with the GAG N-acetyl amide (also 3.5 ppm) at every field (0 Hz separation) - they form one combined amide peak, not separable.
  • The rNOE pool (-3.5 ppm) is well separated from the +3.5 ppm amide but overlaps the semisolid MT pool (-2.4 ppm) at 0.5 T (23.4 Hz) and 1.5 T (70.3 Hz); at 3-7 T the separation (753-1758 Hz) still sits under the huge MT linewidth, so MT/NOE separation is hard and needs multi-pool fitting, not MTRasym.

Direct water saturation: Swept B1 is low (0.25-0.75 µT) with direct-sat bandwidth 10.6-31.9 Hz. The +3.5 ppm amide offset is far from water in Hz, so no direct-sat masking. The -3.5 ppm rNOE is on the upfield side where direct water saturation is negligible; the relevant confounder there is the MT tail, not direct saturation.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: The amide kex=65.5 s−1 is a class-level median of two generic in-vivo brain measurements (PMID 40228056, 23008121), not disc-specific; the rNOE transfer rate 5 s−1 is a phantom/solution class value (PMID 25996515). Disc pH 5-7 and collagen H-bonding shift kex markedly, so the simulated 3-8.5% contrast is an estimate; lower confidence.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 3.354% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 5.527% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Amide kex~65.5 s−1 is slow-intermediate; low-moderate B1 (0.75 µT) avoids direct-saturation loss while 3000 ms Tsat reaches steady state for the slow-exchanging pool. High field separates amide from water in Hz.
    recommended sequence: 6.771% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same slow-exchange physics; 0.75 µT is safe at 5 T and 3000 ms sustains steady state. Higher B0 improves Hz separation of the +3.5 ppm amide from water and aids MT/NOE discrimination.
    recommended sequence: 7.896% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — At 7 T the amide is well separated in Hz from water; 0.75 µT and 3000 ms hold the slow-exchange optimum. Max contrast 8.471% is plausible but the GAG-amide collision means it is a combined amide signal, not APT alone.
    recommended sequence: 8.471% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: B1 0.25-0.75 µT and Tsat 3000 ms suit the slow-intermediate amide (kex~65.5 s−1): slow exchange peaks at low B1 and long saturation to reach steady state. Because the amide collides with the GAG amide and the rNOE overlaps MT, MTRasym is inadequate; multi-pool Lorentzian fitting or AREX/DSP-CEST is needed. PMID 33475842 did exactly this Z-fitting (APT+NOE+GAG+MT) in lumbar discs; PMID 40312958 shows DSP-CEST+AREX separates APT from NOE at 3 T.

Potential clinical impact

No verified disease application of this pool's CEST/NOE signal was found. Searched 'amide proton transfer / APT CEST intervertebral disc degeneration' and 'APT MTRasym low back pain'; only two Z-spectrum/multi-slice CEST low-back-pain studies (PMID 33475842, 42286353) return. The mobile amide pool is not quantifiable by MRS/metabolomics, so no type-(b) metabolite-change studies exist; no studies dropped.

Caveats / critique (6 points, 290 words) — 250 mM amide-proton-equivalent for mobile disc protein is plausible for the annulus fibrosus, but the nucleus pulposus is collagen-poor and GAG-rich; a single 2…
  • 250 mM amide-proton-equivalent for mobile disc protein is plausible for the annulus fibrosus, but the nucleus pulposus is collagen-poor and GAG-rich; a single 250 mM value smears the AF/NP difference. Disc amides are heavily tied up in rigid fibrillar collagen (slow, H-bonded) rather than truly mobile protein, so the 'mobile' label overstates solvation. Wrong concentration means wrong contrast.
  • Amide class and 3.5 ppm are correct for the backbone peptide NH - the canonical APT resonance. Side-chain Asn/Gln amides (~3-3.5 ppm) reinforce it and are correctly folded in. The aliphatic C-H rNOE pool at -3.5 ppm (7H/residue) is plausible for a mobile protein. No amine/guanidinium relied on (fast-exchanging, merged into water), which is fine.
  • No exchangeable proton is clearly neglected. The chemist's claim of a 'clean, high-offset' APT is weakened because in the disc this amide is partly collagen-bound and H-bonded, broadening it. Disc APT sits near 3-3.6 ppm, consistent with the simulated 3.5 ppm.
  • Discs run at low pH (5-7, PMID 27670140), which red-shifts amides and accelerates exchange vs the healthy-tissue reference; the fixed 3.5 ppm / 65.5 s−1 is a healthy-tissue proxy. Backbone amide, Asn/Gln amides, and Lys/Arg amines are the exchangeable groups. Lys/Arg amines and guanidinium are fast-exchanging and merged into water - correctly not relied on as a CEST peak.
  • No distinct exchangeable group is missing. no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor Repeating unit: mobile peptide/protein backbone amide (-NH-). n_exchangeable_protons = 1 per equivalent amide unit. Reported as amide-proton-equivalent (~200-300 mM), NOT as molarity of whole collagen molecules (which would be tiny).
  • Rigid cross-linked collagen excluded from the mobile pool. Concentration per amide unit.

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — axial, centred on the mid-body of the L4/L5 (or L5/S1) intervertebral disc, parallel to the endplates

Why this scan:

  • A single axial lumbar disc level contains five tissues with known, very different GAG and mobile-protein content: nucleus pulposus (high GAG, dilute gel), annulus fibrosus (lower GAG, collagen-rich), vertebral body marrow (negligible GAG, low amide fat), paraspinal muscle (low GAG, high amide), and CSF (near-zero both). One saturation scheme is applied to all.
  • If the 1 ppm (sugar-OH) asymmetry follows the GAG gradient (NP>AF>>marrow/CSF) while the 3.5 ppm (amide) asymmetry follows the protein gradient (AF/muscle>NP), the two patterns diverge, proving offset-specific exchange contrast rather than a uniform MT/NOE background that would look similar across all ROIs at a given offset. CSF and marrow serve as near-zero negative controls.
ROIWhere it is drawnRole

annulus fibrosus target tissuePeripheral collagenous rim of the same disc, anterior and lateral to the nucleus, drawn as a crescent band excluding the nucleus centrally and the vertebral endplate anteriorly.target tissue; lower GAG, collagen/protein-rich

Scan protocol: 3 T, slab-selective rectangular (spatially selective) B1 saturation pulse train, duty-cycled, B1=0.75 µT, 180 pulses × 4 ms (interpulse delay 6 ms, duty cycle 40%), total Tsat=1800 ms, TR=2100 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model):

  • Lumbar spine uses a body coil with large average mass. At 3 T with 0.75 µT mean B1 and a 40% duty cycle, whole-body-average SAR stays well under the 4 W/kg limit even with the ~1.8 s saturation and 2.1 s TR.
  • Local SAR in paraspinal muscle is the limiting tissue; the duty-cycled train (not CW) spreads the deposit over 1.8 s per TR, and a single 2 mm axial slice keeps the excited volume small, so the budget is comfortably met.

Compromise rationale:

  • GAG -OH (high-contrast candidate, ~18% simulated at 3 T) saturates quickly at the physicist's 0.75 µT/750 ms optimum; APT amide wants 0.75 µT/3000 ms. I take B1=0.75 µT to match both, and extend saturation to 1800 ms.
  • This favors the GAG -OH pool (near-optimal, little penalty above 750 ms) and only partially satisfies the slow-exchanging APT amide (under-saturated vs 3000 ms), accepting lower APT contrast. A 40% duty cycle limits steady-state SAR and B0 drift. Saturation (1800 ms) plus readout fits inside the 2100 ms TR.

Fat suppression: SPAIR (spectral adiabatic inversion) prepulse, chosen over SPIR because vertebral body marrow fat is heterogeneous and SPIR is known to fail in T1-short, low-B1 marrow adjacent to the disc. Marrow fat lies directly anterior and lateral to the nucleus and would dominate the 3 T water signal, corrupting the MTRasym baseline; perivertebral and subcutaneous fat also fill the FOV. Verify nulling at the vertebral body and disc periphery with a fat-only navigator.

Motion mitigation:

  • Lumbar spine has no respiratory excursion, so no breath-hold or respiratory gating is needed; the main motion is cardiac-driven CSF pulsation in the thecal sac and slow voluntary body motion. Use a 2 mm slice and short single-shot EPI readout to limit intra-slice blurring; acquire the Z-spectrum in ~2-4 min (18 offsets x ~2.1 s TR plus readout).
  • CSF pulsation is confined to the small posterior thecal sac. No ECG gating needed. Supine with knees supported to reduce lumbar lordosis/muscle tension and a head/neck support for stillness.

Slice coverage:

  • Single 2 mm-thick axial slice (or 2-3 mm slab, 1-2 slices) through the L4/L5 or L5/S1 disc mid-body, centered on the posterior aspect of the disc where the nucleus is maximal, run parallel to the endplates and squarely within the disc space (not the endplates).
  • Axial is chosen over sagittal because a sagittal midline slice captures nucleus+AF+marrow but NOT paraspinal muscle (it lies lateral, outside the midline); the axial disc level captures all five ROIs in one FOV. FOV ~300×300 mm, positioned so nucleus is central, AF anterior/lateral, thecal-sac CSF posterior, vertebral body anterior, and paraspinal muscle posterolateral.

Structures in FOV: nucleus pulposus, annulus fibrosus, spinal cord, vertebral body marrow, paraspinal muscle, cerebrospinal fluid, epidural fat, lumbar vertebral body cortex

Differential analysis plan:

  • For each ROI, extract the ROI-averaged Z-spectrum at every offset and compute MTRasym = (MTR(-d)-MTR(+d))/2 and a Lorentzian-difference curve vs the 0 ppm reference, after a low-power WASSR B0 correction (essential given vertebral bone B0 inhomogeneity) and fat-null verification. GAG test: at ~1.0 ppm (OH) and -1.0 ppm (glycoNOE), NP should show the LARGEST MTRasym, AF intermediate, marrow/muscle/CSF small.
  • APT test: at +3.5 ppm, AF and paraspinal muscle should be LARGEST, NP intermediate, CSF/marrow ~zero. A confirming GAG signature is MTRasym(1 ppm): NP > AF >> CSF/marrow, AND it must NOT track the 3.5 ppm pattern (which is AF/muscle>NP).
  • If NP and AF show similar 1 ppm asymmetry while differing at 3.5 ppm, the 1 ppm feature is more likely generic MT/NOE than GAG-OH and the claim is refuted/inconclusive. Use +/-8 ppm as the baseline zero. Compare MTRasym at 0.7x and 1.3x B1 to bound the transmit-inhomogeneity uncertainty across ROIs.

Not actively targeted:

  • Both provided candidates (GAG -OH pool and mobile protein/peptide APT) were actively designed around; none were excluded. The GAG N-acetyl amide group at 3.5 ppm is folded into the 3.5 ppm APT offset rather than given a separate protocol, so its contribution is read from the same 3.5 ppm asymmetry (expected to reinforce disc-localized APT).
  • The rNOE pools (glycoNOE at -1 ppm, aliphatic rNOE at -3.5 ppm) are captured as their own negative offsets within the single sweep and are not separate protocols.

Caveats:

  • Real limits for this lumbar anatomy: (1) NP is small and central; a 2 mm axial slice through the disc center risks partial volume with the AF rim and endplates, so draw the smallest clean NP-only ROI and verify it excludes AF.
  • (2) Strong B0/B1 inhomogeneity across the disc-cord-marrow-muscle span from vertebral bone, fat, and bone-air interfaces; even after WASSR, residual B0 error shifts the 3.5 ppm APT asymmetry, and body-coil B1 dip varies ROI-to-ROI (hence the 0.7x/1.3x B1 re-simulation).
  • (3) The single-compromise B1 (0.75 µT, 1.8 s) is near-optimal for the fast-intermediate GAG-OH but under-saturates the slow-exchanging APT amide, so APT conclusions are less sensitive. (4) Susceptibility from vertebrae and (at L5/S1) bowel gas can distort the EPI readout; prefer the L4/L5 level and short TE. (5) CSF pulsation and motion limit SNR in the small posterior thecal-sac ROI.
  • One scan cannot simultaneously optimize both metabolites' exchange regimes.
